P1.evidence: No setter notes existed to read back. The frame ran three of the four parts — "I just want to understand what's your situation, what's going on, what have you tried before, and where are you actually trying to get to" — with no "what's in the way" and no "what you need". Frame agreement was properly sought and given: "Sounds good? — Yeah, that sounds great." The scripted open question was replaced with "tell me, like, how well actually do you know Trevor and kettlebell training itself?", which did surface the need but asked about the product rather than about him.

P2.evidence: Much stronger than this rep's other calls on the physical facts. Age and weight were asked directly ("how much do you weigh currently?", "how old are you?") and height came out in the same exchange. Injuries were interrogated genuinely well — "What kind of injuries?", "do you feel like a resistance, any pain in this?", "Did you get like a scan?", "did you go back to a physiotherapist maybe?" — and duration was established at three years. Training week was asked cleanly ("how does your workout routine look like right now?" / "I don't have one") and nutrition was asked and then pushed on ("when you say pretty well and pretty crappy, what does it mean?"). Results from prior coaching were asked. Work was never asked about at all — that he owns a company with many employees came out incidentally at 00:35:48. Sleep and daily energy were never raised, which is a notable omission for a man targeting a 50-hour race without sleep.

P3.evidence: The best-run phase in the batch. The concrete physical goal was already on the table and properly explored. The bridge was asked explicitly — "is it only about the race or is it something bigger?" — and produced the real answer: "My goal is that I can run with my grandkids... I don't want to be the grandpa that's stuck in the chair." The future-state question followed ("five months from now... how do you think, what opens up for you?"), and the rep drove it through to family, identity and legacy: "you're going to be the 70-year-old grandpa, still active and still strong, that they're going to be respecting you." The two-layer reflect-back landed — "You have a bigger why than only this race. This is just the tip of an iceberg." Weaker on the surface-level checks: no single-thing-you-would-change question, no mobility/strength/energy menu, and "who else does that impact?" was never asked — David volunteered the grandchildren himself.

P4.evidence: Run properly and in order. What he had tried came out in full (CrossFit, the Australian online coach, a self-directed barbell regimen). What happened with each was probed — "Did you get any results from that coaching?" — including the rhabdomyolysis. Why it did not stick was pushed on twice: "you said you were following the program, but like 80-20. Why wasn't it..." and "So what's the biggest missing piece over here? Because like, why have been on and off?" David named the gap himself in the script's own vocabulary — "just consistency, that discipline" — and the rep reflected the mechanism back accurately: "You're lacking consistency, then you're trying to get in, you get in hard, and then you get injured, and then you fall off." The explicit "the information isn't the problem" reframe was not used.

P5.evidence: The consequence frame was skipped again. The rep ran the aspirational future — what opens up if it goes well — and never once ran the cost of inaction. No two-year question, no "is that something you're willing to settle for", no "why not". The only adjacent move was the ownership question "who's actually responsible to make that change in your life?", answered "me. Nobody else." This is now the second call in a row from this rep where P5 is entirely absent, and it is the phase whose absence shows up later as a price negotiation.

P6.evidence: Not reachable. The call ended for time before any presentation or commitment check; both were run on the continuation later the same day.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted on this call.

objection_plays.detail: No offer was made, so no deferral was possible.
The wife appears only as someone he would like to enrol alongside him.
No price was named on this call.
No timing resistance; the November race deadline creates urgency in the rep's favour.
No fear or doubt surfaced on this call. It appeared on the continuation.

The most important script gap in this batch. The prospect disclosed ruptured cervical discs with three years of ongoing hand nerve damage, an elbow that physically will not straighten, a torn meniscus with surgery declined, a badly torn ankle and a prior episode of rhabdomyolysis — and the process has no clinical screen, no clearance step and no disqualification path. The rep gathered the injuries diligently, which is to his credit, and then simply carried on toward a presentation. The playbook already records that there is no play for a clinical or medical-fit objection; this call shows the gap is worse than that, because here the clinical objection never even got raised. There is nothing in the process that would cause a rep to stop.

Second gap: the prospect asked whether the programme serves women, wanting to enrol his wife who is managing menopausal weight gain — "you guys deal with any women?" The rep answered "Of course we can" and then honestly undercut it: "me personally, I haven't onboarded a woman. I don't think so." There is no scripted position on whether women are served, by whom, or at what price.

notes: Genuinely good discovery — P3 and P4 were run close to the script and produced a real why and a real root cause, which is what the first two calls of this batch were missing. Two things to fix. First, P5 is missing again; the rep runs the upside and never the cost of inaction, and it costs him leverage every time. Second, and far more important, he collected a catalogue of serious unresolved injuries with care and then treated it purely as material for the pitch. The correct next move after "I ruptured some discs in my neck" and "two doctors said surgery would make it worse" is a clearance question, not a mobility protocol.
